matches.rationale: No finding identifies the inflated dataset size of FT-HID (38,364 vs. the true 9,120) in Table 1 or questions the data provenance for that dataset.

Both identify the same Rodrigues formula sign error in Equation (3): the ground truth notes that (1−cosθ) was replaced by (1+cosθ), and pred 2 explicitly states the coefficient must be (1−cosθ) and points out the error.
No finding mentions the removal of batch size, learning rate schedule, warmup steps, weight decay, or gradient clipping thresholds from the training recipe description.
No finding challenges the abstract's claim of 'first egocentric realistic world simulator' or argues that prior works already explored egocentric scene navigation.
No finding identifies the fabricated 'Matrix-Game [49]' citation; the reference-related findings address different issues (swapped citations, Qwen2.5-VL misattribution, MuZero reimplementation).
No finding reports that the evaluation was silently restricted to indoor scenes, excluding outdoor/dynamic scenarios where performance would be worse.
Both highlight the undefined symbol β in the noise corruption term of Equation (1), making the training objective ambiguous and unreproducible.
No finding points out that enriching captions only for competitors while PlayerOne uses richer motion signals creates an unfair comparison bias.
No finding criticizes the overreach of claiming 'diverse scenarios' and large-margin superiority based on only 100 videos from a single, predominantly indoor dataset.
No finding notes the deletion of the anonymization statement for Figure 1 or any broader lack of ethical disclosure regarding human subjects.
No finding flags the exaggerated promotional language in the introduction (e.g., 'completely solves ... eliminates all limitations').
Both point to a cross-section inconsistency between the abstract's promise of real-time generation and the experimental details reporting ~8 FPS, which is far below real-time.
No finding specifically reports that the final MPJPE in Table 2 was changed to 98.42, nor does any finding contrast that fabricated value with the 127.16 reported in Table 3.
No finding mentions the dimensional inconsistency where zmotion is changed from 3 to 5 channels, causing a total channel count mismatch with the DiT input.

No finding identifies the contradiction between the conclusion's absolute claim of 'ensures coherent world generation' and the documented drop in performance on game scenarios in the limitations section.
